```python
# Logic Analysis for training/stages.py

# Purpose: This module encapsulates stage-specific parameter freezing/unfreezing logic
# for the three training stages (S1.1, S1.2, S2) of NaViL. It provides a utility
# function `apply_freeze_pattern(model, freeze_pattern)` that is called by the Trainer
# before each stage. The function resets all parameters to trainable, then selectively
# freezes subsets according to a list of substring patterns defined in `config.yaml`.
#
# Design assumptions:
# - The NaViL model's named parameters follow a naming convention that indicates
#   whether they belong to the visual or linguistic modality. The MoELLM module,
#   when extending the base LLM with modality-specific experts, must rename all
#   textual (linguistic) parameters to contain the substring "linguistic".
#   Similarly, visual expert parameters contain "visual". Non-expert parts of the
#   LLM (e.g., token embeddings, final layer norm, lm_head) are considered linguistic
#   and must also contain "linguistic" in their names for correct freezing.
# - Visual encoder and connector parameters do NOT contain "linguistic".
# - The freeze_pattern from the stage configuration is a list of substrings;
#   parameters whose name includes ANY of these substrings will be frozen (requires_grad=False).
# - At the beginning of each stage, ALL parameters are first set to trainable
#   (requires_grad=True) before applying the new pattern, ensuring that parameters
#   previously frozen (e.g., linguistic attention in S1.1) become trainable again
#   if the pattern changes (e.g., S1.2 unfreezes attention).

# Mapping of stages to freeze patterns (from config.yaml):
#   S1.1: freeze_pattern = ["linguistic"]
#         → All parameters with "linguistic" in their name are frozen.
#         This includes the entire linguistic MoE (attention & FFN) and the base
#         LLM’s embedding, norm, and head layers (if named accordingly).
#         Visual encoder, connector, and visual MoE experts remain trainable.
#
#   S1.2: freeze_pattern = ["linguistic.ffn"]
#         → Only linguistic FFN parameters are frozen (the linguistic attention
#         parameters are unfrozen). This matches the paper’s description:
#         “the textual parameters within the self-attention layers are also unfrozen”.
#         Note: we assume that linguistic attention parameters have names like
#         "*linguistic.attention*" (not "linguistic.ffn"), so they are not matched.
#
#   S2:   freeze_pattern = []
#         → No parameters are frozen; the entire model is trainable.

# Implementation details for `apply_freeze_pattern`:
#   1. Accept a torch.nn.Module and a list of string patterns (may be empty).
#   2. Iterate over all named parameters of the model (model.named_parameters()).
#      - First, set requires_grad = True for every parameter (reset).
#   3. If the pattern list is not empty, for each parameter, check whether its
#      name contains any of the patterns. If yes, set requires_grad = False.
#   4. Log the number of trainable vs frozen parameters for verification.
#
# Edge cases:
# - Patterns may match partially; we use simple substring containment. There is
#   no need for regex, as the config patterns are simple substrings ("linguistic",
#   "linguistic.ffn"). The dot in "linguistic.ffn" is part of the string.
# - Parameters of the visual encoder/connector typically have names like
#   "visual_encoder.layers.0...." or "connector.mlp.0.weight". These do not contain
#   "linguistic", so they remain trainable in all stages.
# - If the naming convention is not fully adhered to (e.g., some base LLM layer
#   does not contain "linguistic"), it would incorrectly stay trainable. This is
#   an implementation contract for the MoELLM module: it must rename or wrap the
#   linguistic parts such that they carry the "linguistic" substring.
#
# The Trainer will call this function at the beginning of each stage before
# creating the optimizer, ensuring that only the intended subset of parameters
# receives gradients.

# Function signature and pseudocode:
def apply_freeze_pattern(model: nn.Module, freeze_pattern: List[str]) -> None:
    """
    Reset all parameters to trainable, then freeze those whose name contains any
    of the substrings in freeze_pattern.
    """
    # Step 1: Unfreeze everything
    for param in model.parameters():
        param.requires_grad = True

    # Step 2: Apply freeze patterns
    if freeze_pattern:
        frozen_count = 0
        for name, param in model.named_parameters():
            if any(pattern in name for pattern in freeze_pattern):
                param.requires_grad = False
                frozen_count += 1
        trainable_count = sum(p.requires_grad for p in model.parameters())
        print(f"[Stages] Freeze pattern applied: {freeze_pattern}. "
              f"Trainable params: {trainable_count}, frozen: {frozen_count}.")
    else:
        print("[Stages] No freeze pattern – all parameters are trainable.")

# Additional helper: function to retrieve trainable parameters for optimizer.
def get_trainable_params(model: nn.Module) -> list:
    return [p for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad]

# This module can be kept minimal; it mainly exports `apply_freeze_pattern`.
# The freeze_pattern is extracted from the current stage's config (TrainingConfig.stages[stage].freeze_pattern)
# and passed to this function.
```
